legend: Mateo, the owner of Austin's most popular video game store, was in a generous mood one day. He decides to give a gift to each of the n%%ZSMJ0%% people currently in his store and he has n%%ZSMJ1%% distinct prizes labeled 0,1,…,n−1%%ZSMJ2%% to give out. Since Mateo never does anything the simple way, he comes up with the following scheme to give the prizes out.

He gives each of the n%%ZSMJ3%% people in the store unique numbers from 1%%ZSMJ4%% to n%%ZSMJ5%% (inclusive). He then asks everyone to form a line and so the resulting ordering of the people can be written as the sequence [x1,x2,…,xn]%%ZSMJ6%% (where each xi%%ZSMJ7%% is unique and 1≤xi≤n%%ZSMJ8%%). The prize which Mateo gives person xj%%ZSMJ9%% is equal to x1⋅x2⋅…⋅xj−1⋅xj(modn)%%ZSMJ10%%. Unfortunately, Mateo only has one of each prize so he asks you to come up with an ordering of the n%%ZSMJ11%% people so that each person will get a unique prize number.
input: The first and only line of input will contain a single integer n%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤n≤5⋅105%%ZSMJ13%%), representing the number of people in the store.
output: A space-separated permutation of the numbers from 1%%ZSMJ14%% to n%%ZSMJ15%% (inclusive), representing the ordering of people such that each person can get a distinct prize. Output -1 if there is no such permutation.
note: The product after the first person is 1%%ZSMJ16%% so the first person gets prize 1%%ZSMJ17%%.
The product after the second person is 1⋅4=4≡4(mod7)%%ZSMJ18%% so the second person gets prize 4%%ZSMJ19%%
The product after the third person is 4⋅3=12≡5(mod7)%%ZSMJ20%% so the third person gets prize 5%%ZSMJ21%%.
The product after the fourth person is 5⋅6=30≡2(mod7)%%ZSMJ22%% so the fourth person gets prize 2%%ZSMJ23%%.
The product after the fifth person is 5⋅2=10≡3(mod7)%%ZSMJ24%% so the fifth person gets prize 3%%ZSMJ25%%.
The product after the sixth person is 3⋅2=6≡6(mod7)%%ZSMJ26%% so the sixth person gets prize 6%%ZSMJ27%%.
The product after the seventh person is 6⋅7=42≡0(mod7)%%ZSMJ28%% so the seventh person gets prize 0%%ZSMJ29%%.
